subject: Fixing number of polytamous response options

messages.author: 394838c3712aced6
messages.subject: Fixing number of polytamous response options
parts:
I fit a confirmatory mirt model in one sample, and I'd like to cross-validate the fit of the parameter estimates in a second sample. However, in the second sample, the most extreme response option for a few items was not used. As a result, when I specify the same model with the cross-validation data and set 'pars' equal to the model parameters from the validation set, mirt returns an error that the parameter matrices don't match. 

Is there a way to fix the parameters matrix for the cross-validation sample to have threshold parameters even for unobserved values? I can remove the offending rows from the validation matrix, but that is a rather fragile solution. Is there a more robust way to hand this problem?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fixing number of polytamous response options
parts:
If a parameter in a cross-validation set is not uniquely defined, in what sense can you say that you have 'validated' the intercept in the original sample? You may want to simply omit/collapse the sparse category in the original sample to avoid this issue. Otherwise, your results probably won't make any sense (note: there is a way to set the number of unique categories internally with the customK input through the technical list, but just because you can doesn't mean you should). Cheers.

Phil
